evals.name: rate-limiter-choice
evals.prompt: We need an API rate limiter in front of ~40 microservices, 5,000 req/s, must allow short bursts. Which algorithm and where does it run?
evals.expected_output: Token bucket for burst tolerance, placed in the API gateway, counters in Redis with an atomic Lua script, HTTP 429 with rate-limit headers, and the trade-offs against leaky bucket and sliding window counter, citing Vol. 1 ch. 4.
expectations: Recommends the token bucket because bursts must be allowed.
Places the limiter in the API gateway or middleware given the microservice architecture.
Stores counters in Redis and addresses the read-modify-write race (Lua script or sorted set).
Mentions returning HTTP 429 with rate-limit headers.
Compares at least two alternative algorithms with their drawbacks.

evals.name: kv-store-consistency
evals.prompt: Our key-value store has 3 replicas per key. What should W and R be if we want strong consistency but reads are 20x more common than writes?
evals.expected_output: W + R > N; with N = 3 pick W = 3, R = 1 for fast reads (or W = 2, R = 2 as the balanced default), plus the consequences for write latency and availability, and vector clocks or last-write-wins for conflicts, citing Vol. 1 ch. 6.
expectations: States the W + R > N rule with N = 3.
Recommends a read-optimised configuration (R = 1, W = 3) or explains why W = R = 2 is the balanced default, with the trade-off stated.
Explains what happens to write availability when a replica is down (sloppy quorum, hinted handoff).
